extracted.intended_audience: journalists, journalism students, media professionals, and the general public interested in digital journalism
extracted.subtask_description: A general encyclopedic summary of the Online News Association (ONA), its membership definition, major programs (AI in Journalism Initiative), the Online Journalism Awards, annual conference, and the MJ Bear Fellowship — including stated eligibility/selection guidance where given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of "professional members"
rubrics_metrics.description: The association defines "professional members" as those "whose principal livelihood involves gathering or producing news for digital presentation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given include news writers, producers, programmers, bloggers, designers, editors, photographers and others who produce news for the Internet or other digital delivery systems. Other members may include journalism educators, journalism students, business development, marketing and communications professionals in the media and those interested in online journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online Journalism Awards: purpose / scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Online Journalism Awards (OJAs) are a set of global awards honoring excellence and innovation in digital journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OJAs focus on independent, community, nonprofit, major media and international news sites. Winners are announced at the annual conference. The awards were launched in May 2000 and each year feature over 20 categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online Journalism Awards: category examples and prizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories include (examples) Newsletters, Technology Reporting, Social Media Engagement, Online Commentary and Breaking News; select categories come with a cash prize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cash prizes have been provided by supporters such as the Knight Foundation and others. Specific category evolution noted: from 2017–2023 there was an "Excellence in Immersive Storytelling" category; in 2024 the OJAs introduced an award for "Excellence in AI Innovation." Past winners include major outlets such as The New York Times, FRONTLINE, The New Yorker and Al Jazeera.

rubrics_metrics.name: MJ Bear Fellowship: eligibility and selection intent
rubrics_metrics.description: MJ Bear Fellowships are awarded to promising journalists under the age of 30 who have demonstrated — through professional experimentation, research or other projects — that they deserve support for their efforts and/or vision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program began in 2011 with three fellowships and expanded to six fellows beginning in 2019. Fellows may be working independently or for a company/organization. The page lists fellows by year and role (e.g., reporter, producer, engagement editor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual conference: program focus
rubrics_metrics.description: The ONA annual conference and awards banquet features four days of training, networking, exhibits, and career exploration and revolves around trends and key issues at the intersections of journalism, emerging technology, and leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past keynote speakers have included leaders from technology and journalism. The conference is the venue where OJA winners are announced.
